newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Remains of Turkish Cypriot leader's mother exhumed.
newsitem.headline: Remains of Turkish Cypriot leader's mother exhumed.

text.p: The grave of the mother of Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash was opened on Monday for her remains to be taken and reburied in the Turkish-held north of the island, officials said.
Local authorities removed Emine Denktash's remains from her tomb in a Turkish Cypriot cemetery in the coastal resort of Paphos in the Greek Cypriot-populated south of the island.
A group of United Nations humanitarian officers oversaw the exhumation while a Moslem clergyman read prayers, witnesses said.

Most members of the two communities in Cyprus are unable to cross to the other sector since the island was divided by a Turkish invasion in 1974 which followed a Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.

Denktash, who has not visited his mother's grave for more than 30 years, first requested the remains through the U.N. on the island last year. He wanted his mother to be reburied at a family grave in the Turkish-held part of Nicosia.
The Turkish Cypriot leader was born in Paphos in 1924 and his mother died when he was 18-months-old.
"The matter was handled personally by President (Glafcos) Clerides," a government source told Reuters.

"We tabled the request with the authorities which looked favourably at the issue," said Waldemar Rokoszewski, spokesman for the U.N. force which has been deployed on the island since the outbreak of intercommunal violence in 1963.
